content:
I started creating some issue for problems that are also part of the OpenConjecture dataset (which collects conjectures from recent Arxiv papers).
I also created a github label OpenConjecture
I wrote a SKILL.md to help me with creating these issues. With this one still needs to filter for "sufficiently easy to formalise with current mathlib", although it might make sense to even open issue for things we cannot yet easily (i.e. with less than 1000 lines of code) formalise with current mathlib.

It has been greater to see that half of these issues already are getting picked up by contributors formalising them, many thanks, @Will Blair and Anil paliwal!

Even great that the 2 that already got merged also seems to have gotten solved by @Kenta Kitamura !
see FC#4875 and FC#4868. (Of course that needs review that this is solving the intended problem and not just catching a misformalisation)

I think this is very promising, so I propose to add more of those conjectures!

If you want to help there are the following tasks:

  1. create issues for the OpenConjecture dataset (and mention in the id in their dataset to avoid duplicates) possibly using the SKILL.md mentioned above, or a variant of it!
  2. Help formalising: open issues without pr, you can comment before starting working on them and we will assign you, so duplciate work is avoided.
  3. help reviewing them: these prs should contain them

Thanks, Moritz -- this looks great. I’ll help work through some of the OpenConjecture items, and I’ll use the new SKILL.md when proposing additional issues so that the OpenConjecture IDs and duplicate checks are handled consistently.

On a related proposed-but-not-yet-formalized conjecture, I opened #4847: the Lennon–Pittel conjecture on random stable matchings and selected "I plan on adding this conjecture to the repository." If it looks suitable for the project, please assign it to me and I’d be happy to start formalizing it.
